unit: City of Miami building permit + county Class I
qualifier: Miami's code says no seawall may be built, rebuilt or repaired without a Building Department permit, and the application must come with the county's preliminary environmental approval. You also need a Miami-Dade DERM Class I permit, because the county requires one for any work in tidal waters in every city. Big repairs trigger the city's 6 ft NAVD88 minimum height.
detail_rows: City permit :: No waterfront improvement may be constructed, reconstructed or repaired until a permit is obtained from the Building Department - Miami Code Sec. 29-83 | County approval first :: The application must include preliminary approval from the Miami-Dade County environmental department and, where required, title to bay-bottom lands - Sec. 29-85 | Plans :: Owner-builder or licensed contractor; signed and sealed plans, with survey and top-of-wall elevation survey for larger jobs - Sec. 29-84 | Height :: Minimum 6 ft NAVD88 (Miami River and tributaries: 4 ft NAVD88, built to be raised 2 ft) - Sec. 29-89(a)(4) | Substantial repair :: Repairs to 50% or more of the wall length, costing 50% or more of a new wall, or changing elevation along 50% or more of the length must meet current elevation and design standards for the length of the property - Sec. 29-89(a)(5) | Fees :: After-the-fact permits for work done without permits cost four times the fee - Sec. 29-86(a) | County Class I permit :: Miami-Dade DERM must issue a Class I permit before any work in, on, over or upon tidal waters anywhere in the county, including inside cities - County Code Sec. 24-48(1)(d) and 24-48.1(1)(a) | Short form :: Rebuilding or repairing a seawall at the mean high water line or no more than 18 inches waterward of the existing wall qualifies for a short-form application. It also qualifies where existing primary support piles stick out no more than 14 inches, if the new wall is no more than 18 inches waterward of those piles - Sec. 24-48.2(I)(A)(1) | Who decides :: A short-form application limited to seawalls is decided by the Department with no County Commission hearing. Most standard-form applications are now decided by the Director, apart from listed exceptions such as variances - Sec. 24-48.2(I)(B)(1)(iii)-(iv) and (II)(C)(1), as amended by Ord. 25-73 (1 July 2025) | County clock :: Ord. 25-73 Sec. 8 directs the County to issue a Completeness Summary within 10 calendar days of submission and a final decision on short-form seawall applications within 90 calendar days after that summary. The applicant may waive these limits in writing. The County Mayor reported the timeframes apply from 1 Dec 2025 (report to the Commission dated 17 Apr 2026) | No Class I needed :: Sealing cracks and spalls on the cap or face, repairing pilasters, backfilling behind the wall, and limited riprap or sand-cement bags at the toe (no more than 2 ft out) - Sec. 24-48(3)(b)-(f) | Quick approval instead :: Repairing or replacing the cap or the tieback system gets a written expedited administrative authorization, answered within 10 business days, if the contractor submits structurally approved plans from the building authority - Sec. 24-48(4)(f)-(g) | Not a substitute :: A county permit does not relieve the applicant from obtaining all required federal, state and local permits - Sec. 24-48.5(1) | State (FDEP) :: No state environmental permit is needed to restore a seawall at its previous location, upland of it, or within 18 inches waterward of it - Fla. Stat. 403.813(1)(e). The exemption does not cover permission to use state-owned submerged lands or local requirements - 403.813(1) | State-owned bottom :: Work over sovereign submerged lands still needs Board of Trustees permission even when the seawall work is exempt - Fla. Stat. 403.813(1) | Federal (Army Corps) :: A Department of the Army permit is required for structures or work in or affecting navigable waters, either under a nationwide or regional general permit or an individual permit - 33 CFR 322.3(a)

You also need a Miami-Dade DERM Class I permit, because the county requires one for any work in tidal waters in every city. Repairs costing $500 or more per linear foot count as substantial and must bring the wall to 5.7 ft NAVD88.
